CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  October 17, 2022 - 4:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  The regular meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the regular meeting to order at 4:35 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Williams. (Absent:
  Councilmember Madison)

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation recognizing October 16-22,
  2022 as "National Friends of Libraries Week," in the City of Pasadena.
  Tim McDonald, Interim Director of Library and Information Services,
  and Janice Segall, President of the Friends of the Pasadena Public
  Library, accepted the proclamation, acknowledged the work of the
  Friends of the Pasadena Public Library organization in supporting the
  City's library system. Ms. Segall thanked the Mayor, City Council and
  Tim McDonald for recognizing the work of the Friends of the Library
  organization, and advocated for the passing of Measure L.

SPECIAL ITEMS  UPDATE BY FRANK MILLER, BURBANK-GLENDALE-PASADENA
  AIRPORT AUTHORITY, ON THE HOLLYWOOD BURBANK
  AIRPORT

  Frank Miller, Burbank-Glendale Airport Authority, presented a
  PowerPoint presentation providing an update on the project to build a
  to build a 14-gate 355,000 square foot replacement passenger
  terminal at the airport, and responded to questions.

  PRESENTATION BY ASSEMBL YMEMBER CHRIS HOLDEN ON
  THE STATE OF THE STATE

  Assemblymember Chris Holden welcomed Councilmember Jones and
  City Manager Marquez, and thanked Vice Mayor Wilson for his service
  to the City. He provided an overview of his work at the State
  Legislature, including as Chair of the Appropriations Committee, and

Council Minutes  10/17/2022
   summarized the recent bills/laws adopted (infrastructure, funding
  schools and higher education, broadband infrastructure, and a clean
  transportation system); the Governor's 2022 State Budget (state
  infrastructure, transportation system, clean energy, housing goals,
  education, climate change, inflation relief, minimum wage, food banks,
  business tax credits, California Small Business Covid-19 Relief Grant
  program, homelessness, behavioral health challenges, neighborhood
  safety, and protections from impacts from wildfires and drought.
  Assemblymember Holden spoke on efforts to extend the Gold Line to
  Claremont and Montclair. He also highlighted several bills that he
  authored and coauthored (AB 257, Food facilities and employment;
  AB 1604, Civil service: the Upward Mobility Act of 2022; AB 2644,
  Custodial interrogation; AB 2773, Stops: notification by peace officers;
  AB 102, Pupil attendance at community colleges: College and Career
  Access Pathways partnership: county and offices of education; AB
  2617, Pupil instructions: dual enrollment programs: competitive grants:
  College and Career Access Pathways partnership: best practices:
  communications and marketing strategy; AB 2446, Embodied carbon
  emissions: construction materials; and highlighted his support for AB
  1740, Muratsuchi. Catalytic converters; and AB 1613, Irwin. Theft:
  jurisdiction).

  Assemblymember Holden announced that the State Legislature and
  Governor included $5,000,000 for the Central Library seismic retrofit
  project and $3,000,000 for the Rose Bowl for improvements and
  maintenance issues as part of the State's adopted budget and
  presented two ceremonial checks to the City of Pasadena.

  Mayor Gordo expressed thanks and appreciation to Assemblymember
  Holden; and highlighted AB 2723, Holden. Animals: microchips, noted
  the impact this issue had on one local resident, and thanked
  Assemblymember Holden for authoring the bill.

  Vice Mayor Wilson expressed his thanks and appreciation to
  Assemblymember Holden; raised concerns regarding homelessness
  and addiction issues; spoke on the issue of homeless individuals using
  the transit system as a shelter, noting the resulting impact this has on
  ridership for many residents. The Vice Mayor also expressed concerns
  related to drought matters surrounding California and spoke on the
  urgency to address the State's water infrastructure problems now.

  Councilmember Masuda thanked Assemblymember Holden for his
  support and commitment on the future of the Metro Gold Line
  extension to Claremont and Montclair, and eventually to Ontario.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Luka Dowell, Pasadena resident, spoke on the Los Angeles City
MATTERS NOT ON THE  Council incident, spoke in support of Measure H and tenants' rights,
AGENDA  noting the measure is fair for everyone, helps to avoid homelessness,
  and will be a positive impact on Pasadena.

  Raul Ibanez, Pasadena resident, expressed disappointment with the
  lack of the Community Police Oversight Commission's (CPOC)
  inclusion in the selection process of the new Police Chief; stating that
  the City Council suggested the CPOC's involvement when the
  commission was formed, the City Manager's hands are not tied, and
  that the process of involving the CPOC is not prohibited under the City
  Charter. He expressed that failure to involve the CPOC and disclose
  procedural updates to the CPOC in regard to this hiring is a lack of due
  diligence and best practices; which may point to a lack of
  communication between the City Council and City Manager.

  Allen Shay, Pasadena resident, spoke on the Anthony McClain officer
  involved shooting, noted that the District Attorney's (DA) report
  disputes the Pasadena Police's report in its original state, urged the
  City to avoid the corruption and lies similar to the Los Angeles City
  Council, and to pay attention to community voices.

  Adriana Bautista, representing Black Lives Matter - Pasadena,
  provided comments related to the October 6, 2022, Community Police
  Oversight Committee (CPOC) meeting where the Independent Police
  Auditor (IPA) Richard Rosenthal, and guest speakers Inspector
  General (IG) Max Huntsman from The Los Angeles County Office of
  Inspector General and Assistant Inspector General (AIG) Django
  Sibley from The Office of the Inspector General for the Los Angeles
  Police Commission participated in the informational session on the
  process for conducting administrative reviews of critical incidents; and
  expressed disappointment that the CPOC has not been included in the
  Chief of Police hiring process.

  Bert Newton, Pasadena resident, asked that as the City continues to
  plan the future of housing in Pasadena to consider the development of
  higher density neighborhoods, making affordable housing more
  feasible, reducing traffic, the City more walkable, and public transit
  more viable.
